gen-gf-offside-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified, its capitals nearly level with the lowercase. Offside lays down flat, widely spaced letters with curves left open, while the serif body does the patient work of carrying sentences.
gen-gf-offside-general-sans: General Sans moves with a steady pen pressure and an x-height that fills the line. Its smooth curves give Offside, with those open, widely tracked shapes, a sans-serif partner that never competes.
gen-gf-offside-gf-cascadia-code: Offside's curves refuse to close, leaving every round letter slightly ajar. That open, commanding display look is its strength, while Cascadia Code, a wire-thin sans-serif with wide gaps between neighbors, handles the quiet detail.
gen-gf-offside-gf-cascadia-mono: Offside spaces its letters wide and leaves its curves open, with no heavy accents anywhere. And Cascadia Mono, with compact letters standing like pins in a board, wants its size nudged up a little.
gen-gf-offside-gf-julius-sans-one: Offside tracks its letters wide and lets its curves stay open, giving headings a level, commanding beat. Julius Sans One echoes that openness, quietly.
gen-gf-offside-gf-lisu-bosa: Offside draws an o with sides and top equally thick, flat and commanding, with curves left open. Lisu Bosa, a serif, softens it with gentle heavier strokes.
gen-gf-offside-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Commanding, flat and fineliner-like, Offside spreads its open curves wide across the heading. Noto Sans Syriac then adds tall, round-bowled lowercase and easy s turns, so the sans-serif body feels warmer beneath it.
gen-gf-offside-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips well apart and its mean line set high, so text feels open. Offside adds wide, level headings above it.
gen-gf-old-standard-tt-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp, with generous room where its curves meet the stem. Old Standard TT is the pair's real draw, its heavy downstrokes and cobweb-fine upstrokes giving the serif heading a literary pull.
gen-gf-oxanium-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads large and open, with a tall x-height. Oxanium is best at commanding, monoline display letters, while the plain sans body is best at carrying wide-turning s curves without strain.
